3. Objective and optimizer health
Loss windows follow observed epoch cadence. Partial table-coverage epoch losses are retained in tables, without endpoint crosses. The selected receipt determines the included bases; a targeted TabPFN repair cohort does not imply missing TabICLv2 research runs. Numerical and clipping checks are tabulated; the shared schedule is shown once. Negative density NLL can be valid. Peak clipped fraction is the largest recorded epoch fraction, not the trial-wide fraction.

Figure: pd_pilot_loss_pd
PD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 13 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: lgd_pilot_loss_lgd
LGD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 6 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

2. Credit transfer and non-credit retention
Historical objective provenance limits comparison with the corrected main grid. Missing milestones remain gaps; these pilots do not identify a universal optimum.

Figure: pd_budget_horizon_pd_updates
PD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

Figure: lgd_budget_horizon_lgd_updates
LGD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

Figure: pd_budget_horizon_pd_processed_rows
PD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

Figure: lgd_budget_horizon_lgd_processed_rows
LGD budget-pilot changes relative to the same trial and dataset at update zero. Each curve is one base model at the fixed pilot recipe; points show equally weighted dataset means and lines connect recorded milestones without smoothing. Missing scheduled measurements remain gaps. Credit and non-credit panels use distinct dataset sets. The third panel subtracts mean held-out-credit improvement from mean training-credit improvement; positive values indicate greater adaptation on seen tables. This is a between-table transfer gap, not an unbiased overfitting estimate, since the training monitor reuses adaptation rows and table sets differ. Row exposures count repeated rows. Historical TabPFN objective differences limit comparison with the corrected main experiment; these curves do not establish an optimal budget.

5. Objective, schedule and parameter movement
Losses retain separate architecture scales. Optimizer and parameter measurements are tabulated, and common learning-rate schedules share a figure.

Figure: pd_pilot_loss_pd
PD data loss in recorded epochs, averaged within trial and update window before averaging trials. Window width is 400 updates, no finer than the typical epoch recording interval. Markers show observed windows; missing windows remain gaps. L2-SP is excluded. PD uses cross-entropy; LGD uses TabPFN bar-distribution NLL or TabICLv2 quantile pinball loss. Separate vertical scales preserve each model's loss evolution; their numerical magnitudes are not comparable. Epochs with incomplete table coverage are excluded from the curves and retained in the accompanying tables. Markers are thinned for readability; all recorded window means remain in the line and text summary.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

2. Loss, optimization and predictive learning curves
Data loss excludes anchoring: PD query cross-entropy; TabPFN LGD bar-distribution NLL; TabICLv2 LGD mean quantile pinball loss. Equal partition and configuration weights apply to optimization curves; monitoring first gives each table equal weight. Native objective scales remain separate by architecture. Missing support produces gaps.

Figure: pd_optimization_dashboard_pd_tabicl-v2
PD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

PD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

Figure: pd_monitor_dashboard_pd_test
PD. Each recipe first pairs each table's score with its update-zero value, averages repeated partitions within table, and gives tables equal weight. Lines then average remaining recipe settings at a peak learning rate or sampling protocol. The complete planned partition cohort and unchanged baseline table support are required at every milestone. Missing observations remain gaps. Positive changes indicate improvement. These fixed-context monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: pd_monitor_dashboard_pd_ood
PD. Each recipe first pairs each table's score with its update-zero value, averages repeated partitions within table, and gives tables equal weight. Lines then average remaining recipe settings at a peak learning rate or sampling protocol. The complete planned partition cohort and unchanged baseline table support are required at every milestone. Missing observations remain gaps. Positive changes indicate improvement. These fixed-context monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

3. How training choices change the dynamics
Differences are alternative minus reference. References are no L2-SP, all-parameter updates and LR 3e-7. Model-specific loss scales are never pooled; differences in gradient norm are optimization diagnostics, not predictive benefits. Base-model predictive comparisons are shown in the results notebook.

Figure: pd_factor_dashboard_pd_l2sp_lambda_tabicl-v2
PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for l2-sp. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

Figure: pd_factor_dashboard_pd_frozen_v2.6
PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

PD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

4. Applied learning-rate schedule
PD and LGD use the same configured schedule, shown once in the PD training notebook. Initialization has zero rate; log axes only show positive rates.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

5. Parameter movement
Anchored displacement depends on the trainable subset. Freezing leaves family-specific surrounding modules trainable; movement is not evidence of causal predictive improvement.

Figure: pd_trainable_fraction_pd
PD. Trainable parameters divided by total model parameters for each base and adaptation mode. Counts are taken from observed trial provenance; median counts are used where recipes repeat a model. The frozen condition leaves family-specific surrounding modules trainable; it is not the same parameter subset across architectures.

2. Loss, optimization and predictive learning curves
Data loss excludes anchoring: PD query cross-entropy; TabPFN LGD bar-distribution NLL; TabICLv2 LGD mean quantile pinball loss. Equal partition and configuration weights apply to optimization curves; monitoring first gives each table equal weight. Native objective scales remain separate by architecture. Missing support produces gaps.

Figure: lgd_optimization_dashboard_lgd_tabicl-v2
LGD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

LGD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

LGD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

LGD. Lines give arithmetic means across all planned dataset partitions within a recipe, then equal-weight means over anchoring and adaptation settings at each peak learning rate. A missing partition or recipe produces a gap. Only the nonzero L2-SP arm enters the penalty panel. Data loss is the native query objective excluding L2-SP; incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are omitted. Epoch diagnostics use successful-update windows; parameter displacement uses exact milestones. Native losses are never averaged across model architectures.

Figure: lgd_monitor_dashboard_lgd_test
LGD. Each recipe first pairs each table's score with its update-zero value, averages repeated partitions within table, and gives tables equal weight. Lines then average remaining recipe settings at a peak learning rate or sampling protocol. The complete planned partition cohort and unchanged baseline table support are required at every milestone. Missing observations remain gaps. Positive changes indicate improvement. These fixed-context monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_monitor_dashboard_lgd_ood
LGD. Each recipe first pairs each table's score with its update-zero value, averages repeated partitions within table, and gives tables equal weight. Lines then average remaining recipe settings at a peak learning rate or sampling protocol. The complete planned partition cohort and unchanged baseline table support are required at every milestone. Missing observations remain gaps. Positive changes indicate improvement. These fixed-context monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

3. How training choices change the dynamics
Differences are alternative minus reference. References are no L2-SP, all-parameter updates and LR 3e-7. Model-specific loss scales are never pooled; differences in gradient norm are optimization diagnostics, not predictive benefits. Base-model predictive comparisons are shown in the results notebook.

Figure: lgd_factor_dashboard_lgd_l2sp_lambda_tabicl-v2
LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for l2-sp. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for l2-sp. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for l2-sp. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

Figure: lgd_factor_dashboard_lgd_frozen_tabicl-v2
LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

Figure: lgd_factor_dashboard_lgd_frozen_v2.6
LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for backbone freezing. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for peak learning rate. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for peak learning rate. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

LGD. Matched arm means and paired differences for peak learning rate. Each pair fixes the dataset partition, seed and every other recipe setting. Lines average all planned pairs with equal weight and omit incomplete windows. References are no anchoring, full parameter updates, or LR 3e-7. Penalty, displacement and clipping contrasts are tabulated alongside the displayed loss and gradient curves. Native objectives remain separate by architecture; smaller training loss is not itself evidence of improved predictive performance.

5. Parameter movement
Anchored displacement depends on the trainable subset. Freezing leaves family-specific surrounding modules trainable; movement is not evidence of causal predictive improvement.

5. Probability quality, calibration and thresholds
Brier score combines discrimination and calibration; ECE depends on its bins. Regression calibration requires stored predictive distributions rather than point errors.

6. Classical controls, non-credit retention and cost
One main training seed and overlapping adaptation corpora limit independence claims. The non-credit panel is finite and original pretraining overlap is unverified. No recipe winner is treated as an unbiased estimate of future generalization.

5. Probability quality, calibration and thresholds
Brier score combines discrimination and calibration; ECE depends on its bins. Regression calibration requires stored predictive distributions rather than point errors.

6. Classical controls, non-credit retention and cost
One main training seed and overlapping adaptation corpora limit independence claims. The non-credit panel is finite and original pretraining overlap is unverified. No recipe winner is treated as an unbiased estimate of future generalization.

Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v2
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v2.6
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v3
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_tabicl-v2
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v2
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v2.6
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v3
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

3. Credit transfer and non-credit retention through training
Non-credit curves require all four matched partitions per dataset and retain the baseline dataset cohort. These small-context monitors are separate from final five-fold evaluation.

Figure: pd_followup_curves_pd_credit_seeds
PD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_followup_curves_lgd_ood_seeds
LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

4. Endpoint monitors as supporting evidence
Monitor and benchmark figures have distinct identities, captions and data sources. Their score differences are not estimates of seed sensitivity.

Figure: pd_seed_monitor_credit
PD. Held-out credit: 10000-update monitor effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in AUC (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

Figure: pd_seed_monitor_ood
PD. Non-credit retention: 10000-update monitor effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in AUC (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

LGD. Held-out credit: 10000-update monitor effects for the predefined full-update reference, LR 3e-7 and L2-SP 0.003. Effects are Increase in R² (+ better) relative to each model's original weights. Observations match on dataset and training partition before averaging. Each non-credit dataset requires all four matched partitions; credit datasets have one held-out partition. Points are datasets and vertical marks in the difference panel are dataset means. Positive differences favor seed 43; two seeds do not estimate a general seed distribution.

2. Loss and optimization dynamics

Figure: pd_process_pd_tabicl-v2
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v2
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v2.6
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: pd_process_pd_v3
PD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_tabicl-v2
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v2
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v2.6
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: lgd_process_lgd_v3
LGD. Optimization diagnostics at the fixed reference recipe. Each curve is the median of trial-window means for each displayed training seed and sampling protocol across available dataset partitions; counts are retained in the text. Incomplete table-coverage loss epochs are tabulated separately; missing windows remain gaps. Clipping uses a shared percentage range, linear through 0.1% and logarithmic above. Drift follows exact measured milestones. Loss excludes L2-SP and retains the native objective scale, which is not comparable across architectures.

Figure: shared_schedule_pd_lgd
Learning rates evaluated from the recorded campaign configuration using the training scheduler. Each distinct peak-rate schedule is drawn once, pooling tasks only when budget, warmup and decay floor agree. The rate for update u is the scheduler value before that update (index u minus one). The first update has zero learning rate and is omitted from the logarithmic axis, but retained in the table. These are configured schedules; measured epoch-end rates and their sampling intervals are reported separately.

3. Credit and non-credit trajectories at equal updates
One-sample, per-chunk full-pass and per-table accumulation do different amounts of work per update. Missing milestones remain gaps, and empty panels are omitted.

Figure: pd_followup_curves_pd_credit_updates
PD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: pd_followup_curves_pd_ood_updates
PD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_followup_curves_lgd_credit_updates
LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: lgd_followup_curves_lgd_ood_updates
LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

4. Row exposure and matched cost
Exposure counts repeated rows. No interpolation claims equal row or compute budgets. Cost comparisons require all three protocols for a partition; absolute costs accompany their ratios.

Figure: pd_followup_curves_pd_credit_rows
PD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

PD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

Figure: pd_sampling_costs
PD. Ratios to the one-sample trial matched on base, recipe and dataset partition. Only partitions with all three completed protocols enter. Points are partition means and segments are partition interquartile ranges, not uncertainty intervals. Trial time includes recorded monitoring and excludes queueing; it is not billed GPU allocation time. Row exposure counts repeated rows. Absolute costs and peak memory accompany the ratios.

Figure: lgd_followup_curves_lgd_credit_rows
LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

LGD. Fixed-context monitoring changes use AUC for PD and R² for LGD. Seed contrasts match the same table and partition before averaging and require all repeated non-credit partitions. Protocol curves require every planned trial and unchanged baseline table support. Missing milestones remain gaps; panels without any complete matched cohort are labeled explicitly. Row exposure includes repeated rows and does not establish equal compute. These monitors are separate from five-fold evaluation.

5. Supporting endpoint monitors and interpretation
All three experiment-3 arms share proportional PD sampling. Differences from the balanced-PD main reference cannot be attributed solely to pass mode. Table overlap and overlapping training folds limit independence claims.

All three protocols must be available on the same dataset/partition before comparison; non-credit datasets also require all four partitions. Effects use Increase in AUC (+ better). Every arm preserves the same experiment-3 prevalence policy.

LGD. Held-out credit: 10000-update monitor effects and within-experiment protocol contrasts. All three protocols must be available on the same dataset/partition before comparison; non-credit datasets also require all four partitions. Effects use Increase in R² (+ better). Every arm preserves the same experiment-3 prevalence policy.

3. Original and CPT context curves
Primary scores are PD AUC and LGD R². Scores first average the five paired folds within each table, then weight tables equally. Positive differences favor CPT. No figure is generated for a horizon without a complete common cohort.

Brier score, log loss, ECE, RMSE, MAE and elapsed-time gains use original minus CPT; AUC, R² and F1 gains use CPT minus original. Timing includes fitting and validation/test prediction, excludes prior CPT training and queue time, and can be affected by fixed execution order. Fold averages are descriptive, not independent table replications.

Positive Brier effects mean a reduction in error. These are secondary outcomes at natural test prevalence; do not select an arm with them.

No measurements available for this figure group.

4. Interpretation
Compare 2,048, 8,192 and 26,000 total training rows on one fixed large-table pool. The 8,192-row control is reused explicitly from experiment 6. Context and query size both increase; update budgets, not compute or row exposures, are matched. Differences are descriptive for this credit corpus, horizon and two base architectures. These studies do not estimate a corpus-by-episode interaction or an effect of dataset size independent of population identity.

6. Sampling and exposure illustration
Illustration only: a 10,000-row cap, all processed tables and no skipped updates. Actual runs use base-specific caps and training partitions.

Figure: planned_exposure_lgd_1
Illustrative optimizer-step shares using a 10,000-row batch cap, all registered processed tables and no skipped updates. One sample and accumulation share one marker because both assign one update per table visit; full pass assigns one per disjoint chunk. Dataset labels include row counts; the axis gives the total context-plus-query row cap per chunk. Multipliers beside full-pass dots give full-pass step share divided by equal-table step share, not the ratio of total update counts. Green denotes greater and red smaller share; these colors do not imply better or worse performance. Accumulation consumes all chunks whereas one sample consumes one; equal step shares therefore do not imply equal row exposure. Actual training uses the partition's training tables, base-specific caps and may stop mid-traversal.
